author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Oil prices climbed about 4% Thursday as a surge in attacks on shipping intensified concern that supplies could be disrupted through the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea.

At 12:15 p.m. GMT, Reuters reported Brent crude futures up $4.05 at $105.26 a barrel. U.S. West Texas Intermediate rose $3.99 to $100.04, moving above $100 for the first time since May. Those figures are a dated market snapshot, not live prices.

Brent has risen more than 30% from early-August lows as a lasting halt to U.S.-Iran attacks failed to take hold. Iran-aligned Houthi forces seized Yemen’s port of Mocha on Thursday, according to military sources, adding risk near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait while Gulf traffic through Hormuz remained restricted.

Oil prices can reverse quickly as traders reassess military events, shipping access, inventories and demand. The immediate move nevertheless matters for New England because higher crude costs can filter into gasoline, diesel and heating oil. It also complicates the inflation outlook facing central banks and consumers ahead of the Northern Hemisphere winter.
dek: Brent gained about 4% in a Thursday midday snapshot as attacks and restricted shipping raised fears of disruption through two major energy corridors.
headline: Oil jumps to $105 as Middle East tanker attacks escalate
